A decent enough arcade racer, but I can only barely recommend it. The car handling feels very mid to me, and while it works well enough, it never really clicked or felt particularly satisfying. Some aspects of the graphical presentation are not 100% to my taste (e.g. the 2D-ish characters), although that is obviously a personal preference. The biggest issue for me is the gameplay, which became boring pretty quickly. It feels like you're doing the same things over and over, and the repetitive race structure eventually killed my motivation to keep playing. This seems to be a fairly common criticism as well. The customization is easily one of the strongest parts of the game, though, with a huge amount of options for making your cars look and feel the way you want. I had my fun with it, but I stopped playing fairly early and have absolutely no desire to 100% the game. Overall, I would only recommend buying this game when it is heavily discounted.

PS: Give us back the NFS Underground (2) vibes!

(EDIT: No wheel support for Moza, constant issues with game aswell) This game doesn't deserve all the hate, and I was skeptical about buying this game, but it turned out really well! If you want good drift physics, just get drift pro tires! Hate the cartoon effects? disable them in the car customization! Hate having the cops? The cops are one of the main things about this game! Physics in this game are decent, its very fun, good customization, buy it when its on sale, but not for full price. If you're looking for races with police and fun quests, this is the game. (Mods exist such as dlc unlockers, dont let greedy EA know) But yeah this game is fun and underrated, but not good if you're looking for a game with realistic physics, the arcadey physics are fun IMO.

I spent an hour figuring out why my car starts drifting randomly to only find out later that I had an option set to "Tap gas to drift" (press esc in world to see this option). I changed it to "tap on break to drift" and it worked like a charm.
Secondly, you basically drive the same routes through the whole game, which sooner or later gets boring. It gets even worse after you realize that you have already heard the whole playlist and it starts playing all over again.
On the other hand, huge respect to Criterion Games for supporting Ukraine. We appreciate that.

I have over 100 hours in Need for Speed Unbound, and overall I really enjoyed my time with it. The game's unique visual style, driving mechanics, art direction, and especially the Lockdown mode kept me coming back for more. Car performance customization is also surprisingly deep, allowing players to fine-tune their builds for different racing styles.

That said, this game won't appeal to everyone. If you're looking for a classic story-focused Need for Speed experience, Unbound may not be what you're after. However, if you enjoy arcade racing, stylish visuals, customization, and online competition, there's a lot to love here.

One of the best parts of my experience was meeting some great people online and racing together. Unfortunately, since the developers have stopped supporting the game, hackers have become a major problem. I've reported several players through EA Support, but many of them continue to ruin lobbies by using accleration mod, cheating, and disrupting gameplay. The lack of effective action against these players is easily the game's biggest flaw.

Despite its issues, I still think Need for Speed Unbound is a good game that deserves a chance, especially for fans of arcade racing and unique artistic direction.

The game is not hard, it's badly designed. The AI will speed past you, no matter your own speed. The AI does not make mistakes, recovers very fast and will stick to your car. You can not out run them. They are always behind you and ready to leave you in the dust. There seems to be no class system for the cars, in the first two hours the upgrades are too strict to help anyone out. Every race is a struggle and just not fun. It's all about grinding against opponents that can not be beat. From what I saw online, it heavily depends on your first car choice, mess that up and you're done for. And to top it all of: limited resets. You can only restart races a limited time per day, meaning you can't try to learn one race and finish 1st because by then, you might have no retries left.I liked the graphics, the sound & music. The characters where some strange people, but wouldn't have been a deal breaker. NFS Unbound has a really bad balancing and is not fun to play. I'm not gonna grind in a racing game that is somewhat story-driven.Requested a refund, it's not even worth the 50% off that I paid for it. I'll check back in if it's 75% or more off of the full price.

Great graphics, art style, and more. The handling feels amazing, with the way the cars sound and the adjustments you can make and customization being among the best in the series. This is, however, an EA game- it is incredibly poorly optimized, the EA app is always crashing, the game itself likes to not work from time to time. You'll often times find yourself losing a race and your wagered money because the game crashes mid-race causing you to auto-lose. Despite its gorgeous looks, it is not fun to deal with all of its problems, I really wish this game was in a playable state, but it isn't. I wouldn't even recommend it on a sale.

The graphics are almost identical to the previous installments, and the game focuses way too much on visuals, abandoning the original Need for Speed ​​roots entirely. tldr.text: Mixed (61%): players love the story and characters, yet the same theme draws the most complaints.
Price and monetization draw the next most criticism, along with bugs and crashes.
